sections.title: Each child’s today
sections.html:
Each child’s today

The Approvals section starts with a “Today for (child’s name)” card. If you have multiple children, choose one from the row of buttons above.

  • Tasks completed today out of the total scheduled tasks (“3 / 5 tasks done”) and the streak (“Missing a day does not undo progress”).
  • Needs you: a list of tasks waiting for you, or “Nothing needs you right now.” When adjustments are suggested, the card says “N adjustment suggestions for your child’s habits” with a See suggestions button (suggestions).
  • Habits being built (in progress / limit): the number of new habits in their early stages compared with the recommended age-based limit (ages 0–3: 1; ages 3–6: 2; ages 6–15: 3; 15 and older: 4). Going over the limit is only a soft warning and does not block anything.
  • Last seven days: each day is marked “done,” “not done,” or “not scheduled,” along with how your child did it (did it alone, needed a reminder, did it with you).
  • When no habit has a cue yet, the card suggests “Set a cue for the first habit” and links directly to Habits.

This card is always shown. The “How did you do it today?”, “Habit progress,” and “Look back at the week” sections below belong to the adaptive habit programme (currently enabled).

sections.title: Tasks and rewards to approve
sections.html:
Tasks and rewards to approve

The Approvals section has two lists:

  1. Tasks awaiting parent approval: tasks your child marked as done and that you set to “require approval”. Each row shows the task name, child, star reward, and completion date. Approve it to add the stars (and possibly unlock a badge); Reject it without adding stars.
  2. Reward requests from children: what your child requested, the stars already deducted, and when the request was made. Flow: child requests → parent approves → parent gives the reward → done. Rejecting returns the stars to your child (your child’s rewards).

Approving or rejecting a task, and approving or giving a reward, requires the PIN if your family has set one. If your child marks a task complete directly on the parent device, no PIN is needed. If reminders are enabled, the page also shows a “You have N items waiting for review” banner.

sections.title: The “Needs you” strip and approving several tasks
sections.html:
The “Needs you” strip and approving several tasks

This is being switched on gradually; if you do not see it in the app yet, it has not reached your version.

The top of the Approvals section has a Needs you strip that gathers everything waiting for you: tasks to approve, reward requests and habit adjustment suggestions, each with a count. Tap an item to jump straight to where you act on it. When nothing is waiting, the strip says “Nothing needs you right now”.

In the list of tasks waiting for approval, every row has a tick box. Nothing is ticked for you: choose tasks one by one, or tap Select all (up to 50 tasks at a time). The bar at the bottom says how many tasks of which child you have chosen, then Approve N tasks or Reject N tasks. The whole batch needs the PIN only once. A task that was already approved or rejected (for example by the other parent) is skipped and reported, so tapping twice never gives the stars twice.

Once your child is comfortable with the first habits of a habit set (reminders easing off, or settled) and there is room under the age limit for new habits, the strip suggests adding the next habit of that set. Choose Add the next step to reopen the set’s three steps, or Later (hidden for 14 days). The app never adds anything by itself.

If you installed the app to your home screen and turned on reminders, the app icon shows the number of tasks and rewards waiting on devices that support icon badges (not every device does; it shows only a number, never a child’s name or a task). Pressing and holding the icon also offers the shortcuts Approvals and User guide. The web app has no home-screen widget of its own.

sections.title: Record how your child did it
sections.html:
Record how your child did it

The “How did you do it today?” section asks how your child completed each habit today or yesterday, using three buttons: Did it alone, Needed a reminder, Did it with you. This is optional. The answer helps the app know when to gradually reduce reminders (four phases); it is not a score and is not used to compare children. From age 15, your child can choose for themselves, and you can still edit the answer at any time.

The app only asks about recent completions (today and yesterday), a few items at a time; after you record an answer, it shows “Recorded.” If several completions have not been recorded, the progress card reminds you to add more so it can provide feedback.

sections.title: Look back at the week
sections.html:
Look back at the week

The “Look back at this week (5 minutes)” card appears once a week to help the family reflect together instead of reminding your child every day. It includes:

  • One thing to praise: a habit your child is doing consistently.
  • One thing to adjust: a habit that is not yet consistent, with a suggestion to make it smaller or change the time.
  • Advice to add a new habit (when current habits are fairly steady and the limit has not been exceeded) or keep the rhythm for another week.
  • If there is not enough data: a reminder to record “how your child did it” for a few days so the app can provide feedback.

sections.title: Habit progress and suggestions
sections.html:
Habit progress and suggestions

The “Habit progress” section lists each habit with a cue and its current phase: Choosing a cue, Building the habit, Fading support, Habit formed. These are suggestions for supporting your child, not scores. Each child sees up to three suggestions at a time, and each suggestion includes a readable reason, for example:

  • Building too many habits at once → temporarily pause one habit.
  • Several misses in a row → try making it smaller, changing the time, or adding a weekend option.
  • Most recent completions needed a reminder → try a visual cue or let your child set their own reminder.
  • Your child is doing it independently → switch to verbal encouragement and gradually reduce the stars.

Choosing “Later” hides the suggestion for 14 days (saved in this browser). Select the habit to open Habits and edit its cue. The complete set of suggestion rules is in 6. Habit science.

sections.title: Support by week and habit status
sections.html:
Support by week and habit status

This is being switched on gradually; if you do not see it, it has not reached your version yet.

Each habit gets a neutral status label, always with a symbol and words: Not started (no cue yet), Taking shape, Needs support (a suggestion such as stuck or leaning on reminders) and Steady (easing off or settled, with most recent chances done). The label only describes; it never grades your child.

Open Support over the last 6 weeks for week-by-week bars: alone, with a reminder, together, not recorded, not done. The app writes “Support is easing” only when there are at least three weeks in a row of data, the latest week has the child doing it alone at least 20 percentage points more than the first, and the way of doing it was recorded often enough in both. Otherwise it says “Not enough data to say yet”. This is a design threshold with low confidence, and it is never used to compare children.

sections.title: Graduating a habit
sections.html:
Graduating a habit

When a habit has been settled for at least 3 weeks and your child did it alone on at least 8 of the last 10 chances, the Needs you strip offers three choices:

  • Graduate: the habit leaves your child’s daily list and appears under What I can do (for you and for your child). Stars, history and badges already earned stay as they are.
  • Lower stars: from then on the task gives half, then a fifth, of its first stars (never under 1). Stars already earned do not change, and you can restore the first value at any time.
  • Keep as is: hides the suggestion for 14 days.

The app only suggests and never does it by itself. Each month it asks once, in one tap, “Does your child still do this alone?” for a graduated habit: Still alone or Bring it back. You can also tap Undo right after graduating, or Bring it back under What I can do.

sections.title: One change this week
sections.html:
One change this week

This is being switched on gradually; if you do not see it, it has not reached your version yet.

The One change this week card (under “Look back at the week”) suggests only one change to try for 7 days, chosen from the suggestions your child already has:

  • Smaller: renames the habit and describes it as a two-minute version (available for all 47 habits of the framework).
  • New time: moves the habit to the part of the day your child really does it (worked out from when it was completed; it needs at least 6 recent times, most in another part of the day).
  • Together: you do it with your child for a few days; doing it together is not counted as a miss.
  • New cue: opens Manage tasks to edit the cue.
  • Fewer reminders: wait for your child to start before reminding.

Try it for 7 days both applies the change (if one is needed) and records the try. While a try is running or waiting for an answer, the app suggests no other change for that child. After 7 days the card asks “Did it help?” (It helped / Not yet / Drop it). If you answer Not yet or Drop it for a smaller version, the habit goes back to its full version, and the app does not suggest the same idea for the same habit for 30 days. The suggestions under “Habit progress” (stuck, leaning on reminders, settled) also have a matching Try it for 7 days button.

sections.title: Your child’s weekly focus
sections.html:
Your child’s weekly focus

You mark 2 to 4 tasks as “your child may choose” (tick boxes next to each task in the Your child’s weekly focus card). From age 6, at the start of the week your child picks one or two of them as the focus on their own screen and sees progress as “x/7 days”; no account is needed. For a child under 6 you choose together in the card. A child can only choose among the tasks you opened, and can only save their own choice. If your child does not pick, the screen still shows the What I’m practising strip.

sections.title: Manually add or deduct stars
sections.html:
Manually add or deduct stars

Under Family → Children, each child has a Manual star reward/deduction button: enter the number of stars to change (positive adds a reward, negative deducts stars) and a short reason (“Praise for sharing kindly with a sibling,” “Reminder…”). This requires the PIN and is recorded. Use it to recognize things beyond assigned tasks; do not use it to compare children.

sections.title: Statistics, printing, and sharing
sections.html:
Statistics, printing, and sharing

The Statistics section (Today → Statistics) includes:

  • 7-day trend: a bar for the number of tasks completed by the whole family each day; a day with no completions has an empty bar.
  • Print weekly habit chart and Print weekly report: a task table for each day of the week to put on the fridge, and a weekly report (“X of Y completed this week · N points”). Both print through the browser’s print dialog.
  • Your child’s one-sentence journal: review sentences your child recorded by date and export CSV (the file contains your child’s words, so keep it private). This appears only when the journal feature is enabled.
  • Share a positive milestone: preview and then confirm sharing a family message through the device’s share sheet. By default, the content includes no child names, ages, photos, or tasks and contains no tracking code.
  • At the bottom of the page is the danger zone, Permanently delete family data (family owner only; type DELETE FAMILY exactly; see 9).

sections.title: Reminders
sections.html:
Reminders

When parents allow actionable reminders and there are items waiting for approval, a banner appears on the page and, if device notifications are allowed, the browser sends a notification. No reminders are sent while the family is taking a break. Reminders are used only for items requiring approval, never for advertising.
